I want to return to Rattay

You are leaving Henry behind. This game continues with your new character and you can't come back to him. What Henry left unfinished stays unfinished, and the world moves on without him. To play as Henry, load an earlier save.
Henry took the road back to Rattay. In Troskowitz, someone else begins a new life.
Go to Rattay and start the new life
A wayfarer who waits by the tavern wall.
F2: random name. Backspace: delete. Enter: accept.
Type the name and press Enter
Do you have any work for me?
We're not working now. Come back in working hours.
Who you are and where you have worked. No employer takes you on without it. If you lose it, any of them will write you a new one for a few groschen, with no work recorded.
The errand in writing: what to do, for whom and by when.
What I owe for errands I never finished, a tenth of a groschen each.

The date of the new life.
How long each month lasts: 7 days, like the week of a steady job, 14, or the real calendar. It can always go up. It can only go down if today fits in the shorter month.
Day work and the steady job.
What an hour of work pays, in percent of the usual wage: 100 is 1.8 groschen an hour of day work and 0.8 in the steady job. With Realish Economy, a quarter of that.
The experience an hour of work gives, in percent: 100 is 6 points in the main skill of the trade and 2 in the other.
How hungry and tired an hour of work leaves you, in percent: 100 is twice what the game takes on its own, 50 the same as the game, 0 nothing.
Deliveries, pickups and shopping for the businesses.

What an errand pays, in percent: 100 is 1.5 groschen in the same town and 10 to another, and half again for a pickup. When shopping, what is left of the money. With another value, the businesses do not say the amount: the slip does.
Hours of the working day of the place the errand ends at. The clock stops while that place is closed, so 12 hours is more than a day.
Each business asks for an errand to deliver, and another to fetch or to buy, each once every this many days.

What a business needs before it sends you to fetch or to buy, in percent: 100 is 5 deliveries to fetch and 15 errands to buy, or 50 and 80 hours of its steady job. Each errand that runs out doubles it. 0: it trusts you from the start.
The reputation with the business that each kind of errand asks for, in percent: 100 is 40 to deliver, 50 to fetch and 65 to buy.
Points of reputation with the business when one of its errands runs out.
This many errands run out and unpaid in a town, and its businesses report you to the guard. 0: never.
The month stays as it was: today would not fit in a shorter one.
You have no book of trades, and I take on no one without one. I can write you a new one for five groschen, with no work recorded.
There. Don't lose it this time.
Ten hours today. Get to it.
Nine hours left today. Get to it.
Eight hours left today. Get to it.
Seven hours left today. Get to it.
Six hours left today. Get to it.
Too late. There isn't a shift left in this day.
Where's your book of trades? No book, no shift.
You've done your shift for today.
I was hired. I have to be there by half past eight.
As you like. There's no bad blood.
You are Henry again, and the game was saved. To remove the mods, quit and take them out: Henry gets his recipes back.
Go back to the Trosky region first: the quests of KCD2 Life close there.
Henry takes up his own life again...
You are Henry again. For his story, a save from before the new life is safest: nobody has tested whether what the new character did can break one of his quests.
Use this with care: switching between Henry and the new character can break your KCD2 Life save.
The switch did not work: you play the same character as before.

A new lifeHenry's road is behind you. Now you are a nobody in the Trosky region, with a few coins and your own two hands. Work, run errands, keep yourself fed and make a name for yourself, day by day. Each morning tells you how many days your new life has lasted.

A bed for the nightA tired body does poor work. Sleep in any bed, even one that isn't yours, and the day is kept: the game saves when you sleep. Mind whose bed it is, though: not every owner welcomes a stranger.

Honest workOwners and foremen all over the region pay by the hour for an extra pair of hands. Ask them for work in their working hours, and carry your book of trades: it tells them who you are and what you have done. With a good name, a tavern keeper may even take you on for good, with a bed and a meal.

ErrandsEvery business needs goods carried, fetched or bought, each on its own day of the week. Keep the slip they give you and mind the hour written on it: fail them, and you owe them the goods. Do right by them, or work for them, and they will trust you with more.
A fresh lookFiala, the barber of Zhelejov, gives every newcomer to the village their first haircut for free. Pay him a visit if you want to change your looks.
The way back to Henry did not work. Your job and errands are closed, and the new life goes on.
You have 1 fault at work. Three and you are dismissed.
You have 2 faults at work. One more and you are dismissed.
You have been dismissed for your faults.
You left the region and lost your job.
Not yet. Come back in a few days.
Not without a book of trades. Get one and come back.
You already have a steady job. Leave it first.
I have work at a tavern: six days on and one off, with a bed and a meal. Three faults and I am out.
You're drunk. That's one fault. Sleep it off and come back before one o'clock, or it'll be a second.
You're still drunk. Come back before one o'clock, sober.

Six days of work and one off, counted from today, eight to six, at 0.8 groschen an hour. Bed and a meal included. Be here by half past eight: two late days in a row is a fault. Three faults and you're out, and leaving the region counts as walking out on me.

Six days of work and one off, counted from today, eight to six, at 0.2 groschen an hour. Bed and a meal included. Be here by half past eight: two late days in a row is a fault. Three faults and you're out, and leaving the region counts as walking out on me.

Six days of work and one off, counted from today, eight to six, paid by the hour. Bed and a meal included. Be here by half past eight: two late days in a row is a fault. Three faults and you're out, and leaving the region counts as walking out on me.
I need a bed for the night (1 groschen).
I need a bed for the night (5 groschen).
I need a bed for the night (20 groschen).
It's yours until morning. Sleep well.
You can't pay for it. Come back with the money.
You've paid already. The bed is yours until morning.
I need a bed for the night (10 groschen).
I need a bed for a week (6 groschen).
I need a bed for a week (25 groschen).
I need a bed for a week (50 groschen).
I need a bed for a week (100 groschen).
Seven nights for the price of five. The bed is yours.
Your rented bed is not yours any more.
You're late. Do it again tomorrow and it's a fault.
Late two days running. That's a fault.
Not like this. Come back sober.
You're drunk. I'm not giving you work like that.
You came here with no clothes on. That's one fault. Get dressed and come back before one o'clock, or it'll be a second.
You still have no clothes on. Come back before one o'clock, dressed.
Not like this. Come back dressed.
I don't trust you. Earn a better name working around here, then come back.
You have no clothes on. I'm not giving you work like that.
I don't trust you. Go and earn a better name first.
It's late to take anyone on. Come back tomorrow, before noon.
Good. Be here for tomorrow's shift, by half past eight.
Your family got you a steady job at the tavern.
